title: Developmental Motor Delay and Early Screening
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Late milestones, "floppy" or stiff baby, asymmetry, persistent hand preference before about 12 months (suggests weakness on the other side), clumsiness, frequent falls, difficulty with handwriting or sport. Ask about pregnancy and birth, prematurity (correct age for prematurity up to about 2 years), family history, feeding, vision and hearing, regression, and concerns of parents.
working: Developmental Motor Delay and Early Screening
qa: Why correct age for prematurity? Milestones should be judged by corrected age in early years.
What is the Gowers sign? Using hands to "climb up" the legs when rising from the floor, indicating proximal weakness.
Why is early hand preference concerning? It may reflect weakness on the other side.
What is DCD? A coordination disorder significantly affecting daily activities, not explained by another condition.
Best approach for DCD? Task-oriented training focused on the child's goals.

redFlags.Finding: Waddling gait, difficulty rising from the floor using hands on legs (Gowers sign), large calves in a boy
Marked hypotonia with weakness, poor feeding, weak cry
redFlags.Possible concern: Neuromuscular disease (for example spinal muscular atrophy)

redFlags.Finding: Head circumference abnormal or growing rapidly

manualNotes: Coach parents to embed practice in play: tummy time, reaching games, supported sitting, cruising along furniture. Task-oriented, goal-based practice for older children: ball skills, bike riding, handwriting with occupational therapy. Promote physical activity and participation in sport for confidence and fitness.
